text:
jasmine (support): Escalation from Oaklane — streaming responses are cutting off mid-stream with a broken pipe, and the requests are being counted as 5xx for billing. Customer provided request id: req_0a1b2c3d. They say tokens after the cutoff were still billed.

jasmine (support): Customer repro + example curl they ran:
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \\n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=redwood-alpha \\n  -d '{"prompt":"long streaming test","max_tokens":2000}'
```

oaklane-support (customer): Repro steps are simple — we stream a 5k token response, after ~30s the stream cuts with: `send() failed: Broken pipe`. Our client sees EOF and we treat as user abort; you billed the request as 5xx. We attached tcpdump and Node client logs.

ingrid (eng-runtime): Thanks — can you paste the exact request_ts and gateway_request_id? Also want the tcpdump pcap (we'll need to check FIN vs RST). If customer can share client library version that helps.

kevin (support): customer provided gateway_request_id: gw_20260317_0a1b2c3d and client user-agent: `OaklaneAgent/2.1.4 node-fetch/2.6`. They attached a pcap and Node logs.

mario (eng-sre): I pulled gateway metrics around gw_20260317_0a1b2c3d — there was a brief spike in connection churn at 2026-03-17T02:14:32Z and a backlog on the streaming workers. Nothing catastrophic but a 20s tail latency increase on the proxy pool.

mario (eng-sre): From quick grep of proxy logs: we logged `upstream prematurely closed connection` for that gw id. That currently maps into our 5xx classification in the billing pipeline.

ingrid (eng-runtime): Two hypotheses: 1) client is closing connection (client-side FIN) and we incorrectly mark as server 5xx because trailer/termination wasn't observed, or 2) our sidecar/chunk flusher emitted a half-chunk and the proxy tore down then we reported upstream error. Need to check TCP flags in pcap.

kevin (support): Customer says they did not call abort; their logs show `write ECONNRESET` from remote at same time. They use CloudFront in front of their app.

ingrid (eng-runtime): Can you upload the pcap to /shared/pcaps/gw_20260317_0a1b2c3d.pcap? I'll run `tcpdump -r` and look for RST vs FIN. If it's RST from our side that's bad.

mario (eng-sre): Also FYI a config change rolled 03/15 touched the chunked flush interval on the streaming sidecar (flush_interval_ms from 50 -> 20). svc-ci-deploy-bot shows the rollout completed 03/15 04:12 UTC.

svc-ci-deploy-bot: Deployment record: streaming-sidecar v1.14.3 -> v1.15.0. Flag `chunked_flush_ms` changed from 50 to 20. Canary passed.

ingrid (eng-runtime): That change could increase IO bursts and expose race in proxy's chunk-termination handling. Mario — can you correlate churn spikes with sidecar rollouts?

mario (eng-sre): Yes — the churn we saw started 03/15 and sporadic spikes line up with the rollout window. Not conclusive but suspicious.

kevin (support): Customer asked about billing reversal for the affected calls. Invoice id INV-OKL-20260317 included the disputed charges. Billing wants the ledger id and the exact time window.

billing-bot: To consider an adjustment we need: customer id, invoice id, list of request ids (or time window). Please open an internal billing case and tag @billing-team.

kevin (support): Added evidence to internal billing case BIL-3297 and linked gw_20260317_0a1b2c3d plus a wildcard for 2026-03-15..2026-03-17.

ingrid (eng-runtime): I ran the pcap. Findings: sequence shows our side sent a partial chunk then received a TCP RST from the proxy process (not the customer). The flow: we sent CHUNK (no trailer), then within 100-200ms the proxy reset the downstream. That indicates the proxy side gave up waiting for full trailer and issued RST — likely our chunked framing changed timing.

ingrid (eng-runtime): Conclusion: our side triggered proxy reset -> the gateway marked upstream as error -> billing pipeline classified as 5xx. This is an internal regression.

mario (eng-sre): Immediate mitigation: revert sidecar flush_interval to 50ms for the affected colo pools and add a metric rule to exclude `upstream prematurely closed connection` originating from gateway-proxy restarts from billing pipeline until we fix. I'll schedule the revert canary now.

svc-ci-deploy-bot: Rollback job queued: streaming-sidecar -> v1.14.3. Canary target: 10% edge pool. ETA 12m.

kevin (support): Told Oaklane we're investigating and queued a provisional credit request. Asked for permission to adjust invoice if internal confirms regression.

billing-bot: Billing team pre-approved provisional pro-rate if internal postmortem confirms regression root cause is our side. Please attach postmortem link.

ingrid (eng-runtime): Long-term fix: make chunked flusher behavior tolerant to backpressure and ensure proxy treats client-initiated closes vs internal resets differently. Also update billing classifier to consult proxy origin flags before labeling 5xx for streaming truncations.

jasmine (support): Summarizing action items: 1) Mario to rollback sidecar flush change and add metric exclusion for billing (in progress). 2) Ingrid to own runtime patch and spec for classifier change. 3) Kevin to coordinate billing case and provisional credit for Oaklane. 4) Follow-up postmortem and customer communication template (I'll draft).

kevin (support): Oaklane confirmed they want a billing adjustment if we confirm. They've paused traffic to their streaming test for now — will re-open once we say it's fixed.

mario (eng-sre): Rollback started. Canary logs show no more `upstream prematurely closed connection` events in the canary group after rollback. Monitoring will run 2 hours.

ingrid (eng-runtime): I'll prepare a minimal repro that deliberately toggles flush interval to reproduce locally and get a unit/regression test in CI.

jasmine (support): Thanks everyone — I'll keep Oaklane updated and will post postmortem link here once done. :thumbsup:
